item.title: [Shortcut Guide] Default "Hold Windows key" behavior interferes with Win+V and Win+H
item.author: MichaelGHUser

judgment.rationale: The issue is marked reproducible and explains Shortcut Guide hold activation foregrounding over Windows shell shortcuts/hold gestures; PowerToys can mitigate by suppressing hold UI during Win-key chords even if shell flyouts close by Windows design.
evidence: Reporter reproduces with default Hold Windows key; disabling it avoids the issue.
Maintainer marked Status-Reproducible and noted shell flyouts close when Shortcut Guide foreground closes.
A later comment adds the Windows 11 hold-Win pointer feature conflict.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a Shortcut Guide hold-trigger policy fix and confirm whether the default hold gesture should remain enabled.

fix_assessment.rationale: Reproducible and likely mitigable in PowerToys, but default UX policy needs maintainer confirmation.

proposed_fixes.title: Suppress Shortcut Guide hold UI during Windows-key chords
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Shortcut Guide treats prolonged Win-key hold as activation even while the user is completing a built-in Win shortcut or OS hold gesture.
plan: Cancel hold activation after any non-modifier key in the cycle.
Consider making hold-Win opt-in or requiring an extra modifier if OS hold gestures remain conflicted.
Add Win+V, Win+H, and hold-Win pointer regression tests.
verification: Win+V and Win+H remain usable when held past threshold.
Plain Win-only hold still opens Shortcut Guide if enabled.

confidence.rationale: Focus mechanism is known, but product policy determines exact UX fix.

issue_context.summary: Shortcut Guide default Windows-key hold activation interferes with Windows shell shortcuts and hold gestures.
known_information: Reporter provided numbered Win+V/Win+H repro on Windows 11 25H2 with PowerToys 0.101.2362.
Disabling Hold Windows key avoids the bug.
inferences: Suppressing hold UI for Win-key chords is safer than trying to keep shell flyouts alive.
issue_context.analysis: Shortcut Guide should not foreground its UI for key sequences that are OS shortcuts.
initial_investigation: Reviewed duplicate suggestions #15874 and #49990 from triage comment.
Focused source search identified ShortcutGuide hold/Win-key area for full implementation pass.

information_gaps.information: Maintainer/product decision on whether hold-Windows-key should remain default or become opt-in/extra-modifier.
information_gaps.why_needed: Determines targeted suppression vs setting/default change.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Maintainer comment confirming desired Shortcut Guide default behavior.

design.root_cause: Hold activation is not cancelled after a Win-key chord begins.
evidence: Reproducible report and maintainer focus explanation.

affected_files.purpose: Shortcut Guide hotkey/hold activation and UI foregrounding

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Win-key hold can activate while invoking Win+V/Win+H.
implementation_steps.change: Cancel hold activation for the current Win-key cycle once a non-modifier key is pressed.
implementation_steps.code_block: onWinDown pending=true; onNonModifier while pending suppress=true; onHoldTimer if !suppress showGuide(); onWinUp reset;
edge_cases: Win+Shift+/ Shortcut Guide activation still works.
Win-only hold still works when enabled.
tests: State-machine tests for Win-only, Win+V, Win+H, and Shortcut Guide activation chord.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Hold Windows key is a default behavior.
implementation_steps.change: If approved, update wording/default/migration for hold behavior.
implementation_steps.code_block: if holdWinKeyEnabled show conflict guidance or opt-in state;
edge_cases: Do not silently change existing user settings without migration decision.

verify: Manual Win+V, Win+H, hold-Win pointer tests.
risks: Over-suppression could make Shortcut Guide less responsive.
alternatives: Documentation-only workaround rejected because default breaks common shortcuts.

comment.body: This is reproducible and the current workaround is disabling Shortcut Guide **Hold Windows key**. Could a maintainer confirm whether PowerToys should suppress hold-triggered Shortcut Guide whenever another key is pressed in the same Win-key chord (Win+V, Win+H), or whether the hold behavior should become opt-in / require an extra modifier?
